card.summary: The Child Care Modernization Act of 2026 amends and reauthorizes the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 through fiscal year 2031. It updates definitions for eligible children and activities, requires states to use a cost-estimation model for provider payment rates over time, establishes new supply and facilities grants for child care providers, and mandates additional state reporting and reviews of health and safety requirements.
card.title: Child Care Modernization Act of 2026

summary: The Child Care Modernization Act of 2025 updates and reauthorizes the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990. The bill establishes new authorization levels for appropriations through fiscal year 2030, sets requirements for state plans regarding child care payment rates and cost estimation models, expands definitions for eligible activities and children, and creates a new grant program focused on child care supply and facilities.

affected_groups.effect: May experience modified eligibility criteria, sliding fee scales for copayments, and greater access to consumer education and child care options through mixed delivery systems.
affected_groups.group: Working parents and families with children under 13

affected_groups.effect: Eligible providers may receive subgrants for startup, expansion, and facility improvements, as well as benefit from updated state payment rates based on cost estimation models.
Required to update state plans, consult with local stakeholders, establish benchmarks, and submit new reports regarding child care supply and costs.
affected_groups.group: State lead agencies and tribal organizations

key_provisions: Authorizes appropriations for the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act programs for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
Updates definitions relating to eligible activities, eligible children, family child care providers, and mixed delivery systems.
Requires States to develop and use statistically valid and reliable cost estimation models to set direct payment rates for child care providers by a specified deadline.
Establishes a new Part II for Child Care Supply and Facilities Grants to expand provider capacity, support startup and supply expansion, and fund facility renovations or construction.
Requires States to submit additional reports and progress updates to the Secretary regarding affordability, family income spent on child care, and benchmarks related to the program.
missing_information: Specific dollar amounts authorized for appropriations for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
Specific details on the exact structure of federal allocations to individual states under the new grant programs.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Child Care Modernization Act of 2025 updates and reauthorizes the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990. The bill establishes new authorization levels for appropriations through fiscal year 2030, sets requirements for state plans regarding child care payment rates and cost estimation models, expands definitions for eligible activities and children, and creates a new grant program focused on child care supply and facilities.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation modifies federal block grant funding and requirements for state-administered child care programs, impacting the funding mechanisms, facility development, and operational standards used by states and child care providers across the country.
